newsitem.title: UK: Nike ad criticised for violence.
newsitem.headline: Nike ad criticised for violence.

text.p: A TV ad for sportswear company Nike Inc starring footballer Eric Cantona, has been condemned for its "violence" by the head of FIFA - football's ruling body - the British Press Association said on Tuesday.
Cantona is French and plays for British football club Manchester United.
FIFA's secretary general Sepp Blatter said in the latest edition of its official magazine FIFA News that "FIFA is not happy with an advertising trend that glorifies violence or bad taste".
Blatter did not mention Nike by name but a FIFA spokesman confirmed that it was the ad in question.
The Nike campaign which has been shown around the world, features Cantona and other football stars in a football battle against a host of devils, ghouls and monsters.
Blatter said that "such a style does nothing to promote values especially among impressionable youngsters."

However, Nike denied that the ad condones violence. A spokesman said "The name of the ad was "Good versus Evil" and it was about footballers from all over the world uniting to overcome something bad. It was certainly not about encouraging violence and we as a company know that violence has no place in the game."
Blatter's comments were included in an article on the values of fair play. The organisation is holding a world wide "Fair Play Day" next September.
